title: Quaint Crisp Peruvian Pork Suspiro Limeno
description: A jammy and crisp Peruvian dish featuring minced pork, inspired by the traditional Suspiro Limeno, with a comforting twist, this recipe is also Buddhist-temple-friendly as it does not include any forbidden ingredients.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the minced pork, chopped onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger, mixing well with your hands or a wooden spoon until just combined.
Add the soy sauce, chopped aji amarillo pepper, potato starch, salt, and black pepper to the bowl, mixing until the ingredients are evenly distributed.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Using your hands, shape the pork mixture into small patties, about 1 1/2 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick.
Add the patties to the skillet, being careful not to overcrowd, and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until they are cooked through and crispy on the outside.
Remove the cooked patties from the skillet and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain any excess oil.
Serve the quaint crisp Peruvian pork suspiro limeno hot, garnished with chopped scallions.
Traditionally, suspiro limeno is served as a dessert, but this savory version is perfect for a weeknight dinner.
You can also serve it with your favorite sides, such as steamed vegetables or a simple salad.
